purpose: The page frame for a task that needs two things on screen at once, with neither subordinate to the other: a payment file beside its validation report, a document beside its history, a monitor above its log. The user, not the layout, decides how the room is divided, and the division is published as a percentage so it survives a resize and an axis change.

$cardinalRule: ★★ COMPOSE, NEVER RE-DRAW. The outer frame is a WHOLE SHELL (App-shell-top-nav) rather than a set of atoms, and the body is Splitter. Every region is named in $copiedFrom so a reviewer can diff it. NO PARENT FILE WAS EDITED.

$finding-axis-is-a-token: ★★ THE AXIS IS A CSS CUSTOM PROPERTY AND THE SCRIPT READS THE COMPUTED VALUE, NOT THE ATTRIBUTE. `--axis: x|y` is written by the container query; getComputedStyle(sp).getPropertyValue('--axis') decides the key map, the published aria-orientation and the measurement axis. Splitter's own script read `sp.dataset.orientation` ONCE at wire time, which is correct for a component that never changes axis and wrong for a shell that does. Branching on the attribute would let the CSS and the script disagree the instant the query fired — the class of bug no gate can see. A ResizeObserver re-reads it and re-publishes. MEASURED across three container widths: 1352 -> axis x, tracks '638px 8px 638px', aria-orientation vertical · 852 -> axis y, tracks turned, aria-orientation horizontal · 512 -> display flex, divider display:none, tabbable separators 0.
$finding-coequality-is-constructed: SPLIT IS NOT MULTI-COLUMN AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ENFORCED, NOT ASSERTED. Multi-column is a ranked master-detail cascade; a split is two peers. Coequality is checkable and was checked: ONE `.sh-pane` class used twice (`.is-primary` count in the document = 0), pane head heights [48, 48], and --min-pri == --min-sec == 240px. A reviewer who wants one pane subordinate wants App-shell-multi-column.
$finding-separator-removed-on-phones: THE SEPARATOR IS REMOVED BELOW 600cqi AND THAT IS AN ACCESSIBILITY DECISION, NOT A LAYOUT SHORTCUT. `display:none` takes it out of the accessibility tree as well as the picture. A drag-to-resize control is unusable by touch at phone size and offers arrow-key adjustment to a user with no arrow keys. MEASURED at a 392px container: tabbable separators = 0. The alternative (keep it, shrink it) was drawn and rejected. ⚠ A consequence, declared: a hidden separator publishes nothing, so its authored aria-orientation attribute goes stale — harmless, because a display:none element is not in the tree, but it is a stale attribute and it is named rather than tidied.
$finding-hit-area-caught-by-driving: ⚠ A REAL DEFECT, FOUND BY A DRIVEN HIT-AREA SWEEP AND BY NOTHING ELSE. The pane-head action buttons were authored 36x36 to sit inside a 48px band. 36px clears WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor and EVERY GATE IN THIS REPO WAS GREEN OVER IT, because no gate reads target/min for hit area — the same blind spot App-shell-top-nav found on Breadcrumbs. A 44px control fits a 48px band with 2px to spare, so there was never a reason to shrink it. Measured before 36.0 x 36.0, after 44.0 x 44.0, and the post-repair sweep names only the two separators.
$finding-separator-target-inherited: THE 24px SEPARATOR TARGET IS SPLITTER'S OWN INHERITED-RESTRAINT CALL, CARRIED UNCHANGED AND DECLARED. Every other interactive element in this file measures >= 44px. The separator's ::before is 24px, which meets WCAG 2.5.8 and not the repo's own target/min. That divergence belongs to the parent; it is not repaired here and it is named as an open question.
$finding-type-divergence: No raw font-family, font-size or font-weight appears anywhere in component scope; every text element carries a canon/type.css composite applied in the MARKUP (the T-D14 route). Probe: `python3 knowledge/_validate_type_composites.py | grep -c App-shell-split` -> 0, with the total reading exactly 1097. Ratchet contribution: 0.
$finding-breakpoints-unruled: ⚠ 900cqi AND 600cqi ARE SPECIMEN CHOICES, NOT RULED BREAKPOINTS, and this file DELIBERATELY REUSES App-shell-top-nav's pair rather than choosing a fourth. Wave 5 shipped three shells with three different pairs (900/600, 1040/720, 1200/840) and named that as its biggest open question; adding to the spread would have made it worse. Probe: python3 -c "import json;print('breakpoint' in json.dumps(json.load(open('knowledge/tokens/layout.json'))).lower())" -> False.

$relationshipsNote: May legitimately contain an Action-bar inside either pane — a pane's own action row is not the site footer, and the two can appear together. The 'footer' vocabulary collision Footer's meta declares applies here unchanged.

accessibility.landmarks: One <header>, <nav aria-label="Primary">, <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">, <main>, <footer role="contentinfo">. Each pane is a <section aria-labelledby> pointing at its own <h2>.
accessibility.separator: role="separator" with tabindex=0, aria-controls naming the pane it sizes, aria-valuemin/max/now and an aria-valuetext that reads as a percentage. The published value is a PERCENTAGE of the container, so it survives a resize; aria-orientation is re-published whenever the container query turns the axis.
accessibility.keyboard: Arrow keys step 16px (64px with Shift) along the live axis; Home and End run to the fences; Enter collapses and restores; F6 recentres. MEASURED: 50 -> 55 after four ArrowRight; Home lands on 19, not 0, because the 240px fence wins — which is the proof the two input paths share one clamp.
accessibility.bypassBlock: A skip link is the first focusable element, visible only on focus, targeting <main>. SC 2.4.1.
accessibility.disclosure: The menu button carries aria-expanded + aria-controls; the sheet is role=dialog aria-modal with the background inert. MEASURED at 420px: closed {tabbableOutside 10} -> open {focusInSheet true, active 'Close main menu', tabbableOutside 0} -> Escape {active 'Open main menu', tabbableOutside 10}.
accessibility.targetSize: Every interactive element measures >= 44px EXCEPT the separator, whose ::before is 24px — Splitter's declared inherited-restraint call, carried and named. Driven sweep after repair returns only the two separators.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: Links are underlined, not coloured. The current destination is marked by shape and surface as well as hue. The separator carries a grip SHAPE as well as a contrast change.
accessibility.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses every transition to 0.01ms. The divider itself is deliberately not animated at any setting — a dragged thing that lags its pointer is a broken thing.

responsive.mechanism: CONTAINER queries on the shell (container-type:inline-size, container-name:shell), never viewport queries. s210-D3. ⚠ Every rule targets a DESCENDANT of .sh; an element is a query container for what is inside it and never for itself, and a rule that forgets this never fires while looking entirely plausible in a screenshot.
responsive.full: >= 900cqi — side by side, a vertical divider the user can drag. MEASURED at a 1352px container: tracks '638px 8px 638px', separator tabbable.
responsive.compact: 600–899cqi — the panes STACK, the same divider becomes horizontal, the same percentage is preserved, aria-orientation and the key map turn with it. MEASURED at 852: axis y, tracks turned, aria-orientation 'horizontal'.
responsive.phone: < 600cqi — the divider is removed from the page and from the a11y tree, the panes fall to natural height in document order, and the shell scrolls as one column. MEASURED at 512 and at a 392px container inside a 1400px viewport: display flex, divider display:none, tabbable separators 0.
responsive.$proof: The third specimen is a 392px CONTAINER at the same viewport as the two wide ones and it is fully collapsed while they are not. That is the container-not-viewport proof, in one still.

dimensions.$note: mastheadHeight 64 is Navigations'. dividerThickness 8 and the 24px pointer target are Splitter's. paneMinimum 240 is this file's and it is SYMMETRIC on purpose — Splitter ships 160/160; a pane carrying a table needs more, and both panes get the same more.

antiPatterns: Never use a split where one pane drives the other. That is App-shell-multi-column, and it has a rail, a list and a detail for a reason.
Never give the two panes different chrome. The moment one has a toolbar the other lacks, the user reads it as the important one and the component has become something else.
Never make the fences asymmetric. An asymmetric fence is a ranking expressed in pixels.
Never publish the divider's position in pixels. Pixels do not survive a resize, an axis change, a hidden tab panel or a print stylesheet — the percentage is the thing the user chose.
Never keep a drag-to-resize separator at phone width. It cannot be operated by touch with any precision and it offers arrow keys to a device that has none.
Never put a third pane in. A split is two.

$decisionsForDave: 1 · THE BREAKPOINT SCALE, and it is the wave's biggest open item rather than this file's. layout.json has no breakpoint scale. This lane's four shells all reuse App-shell-top-nav's 900/600 pair rather than adding to wave 5's three-way spread — but reusing an unruled number is not the same as having one.

2 · DOES A SHELL BELONG IN knowledge/snippets/ AT ALL? Carried from wave 5 unchanged. The evidence for is that the existing gates watch these files for free and caught two real defects in this lane. The evidence against is that the showroom, the KG and component-types.json all assume components.

3 · THE SEPARATOR AT PHONE WIDTH. Drawn as removed entirely — from the picture and from the accessibility tree. The alternatives are: keep it and shrink it; keep it and make it keyboard-only; replace it with a preset 50/50 – 70/30 control. Removal is PROPOSED, not ruled.

4 · SHOULD SPLITTER ITSELF GROW 44px ON ITS SEPARATOR? Its ::before is 24px by an inherited-restraint argument. Every other control this repo ships is 44. A worker lane could not touch a gated file to find out.
5 · SHOULD THE AXIS-AS-A-CUSTOM-PROPERTY PATTERN GO BACK INTO Splitter? It is strictly more general than reading the attribute once, and any splitter that ever meets a container query needs it.

6 · WHAT ARE THE TWO PANES CALLED? Drawn as 'Uploaded file' / 'Validation report' and 'Run monitor' / 'Event log'. Every one is placeholder domain prose, PROPOSED under s182-D2, and none is a semantic this lane is entitled to mint.
7 · SHOULD THE SPLIT REMEMBER ITS POSITION between visits? The percentage is the right unit to persist, but persistence is a product decision and nothing here writes storage.
